statements.text: AI innovation must benefit everyone, not simply help tech industry giants at the expense of working families. We must protect U.S. jobs and the American workforce during the transition.
statements.venue: US Senate candidate questionnaire (attribution to Stratton inferred)

statements.text: Well, certainly we want Illinois to be on the cutting edge of new technologies. And certainly AI and the advancements that are possible can be exciting, and we want to be a part of that. But we have to think about jobs.
statements.venue: Illinois U.S. Senate Democratic primary debate (C-SPAN transcript)

statements.text: But one thing that we know, that as we move this forward, we have to make sure we think about workers and not allow AI or any technology to take away the opportunities for people to get good paying jobs.
statements.venue: Illinois U.S. Senate Democratic primary debate (C-SPAN transcript)

statements.text: And so I think overall we have to make sure that there are guardrails, guardrails that don't allow corporate greed to come in and say we're going get rid of an entire division of employees because we think it's going to be more economical for us to just use AI.
statements.venue: WTTW Chicago Tonight U.S. Senate Democratic candidate forum

statements.text: Artificial intelligence is creating incredible opportunities, but it also brings new risks, especially for young people. Illinois is showing that innovation and accountability can go hand in hand by setting clear expectations that help protect our communities while supporting the responsible development and use of AI. We can embrace emerging technology while ensuring it reflects our values, safeguards the public, and helps build a stronger future for everyone.
statements.venue: Statement on Illinois AI safety law signing, reported by Route Fifty

statements.text: We have a duty to the people of Illinois to make sure any technology being rolled out is safe and regulated — that includes artificial and super intelligence. While innovations like this have the capacity to improve our lives, they also have the capacity to do real harm. We must act now to put the proper guardrails in place to get Big Tech out of our elections, hold Washington accountable, and ensure that Illinoisans are protected as we continue to innovate.
statements.venue: Governor's office press release on AI safety (as Lt. Governor)

statements.text: Well, we have to be a leader and we need guardrails. [...] So there's a possibility for immense real innovation that we can see come from AI, but also there's immense harm that can come from AI, and we are hearing that every single day of what's possible. [...] We need some federal guardrails, and we'll see what's proposed in terms of what that looks like. And then we again need to include the global community as well, because this is something that will affect all of us.

Look, what I've always said is that they have to pay their fair share. And what that means to me is they have to make sure that their investments in the electric grid so that we have reliable electricity — they have to make sure that they are making investments and not taking away from the fact that there are also consequences to our natural resources. [...] It cannot be something where Illinoisans have to shoulder the burden for the expansion, and that's what I want to see.
statements.venue: Illinois Public Media (WILL) interview, on data centers
